newsitem.title: INDIA: India Congress drive against Rao picks up steam.
newsitem.headline: India Congress drive against Rao picks up steam.

text.p: Indian Congress party legislators stepped up their campaign on Tuesday to remove former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, tainted by corruption charges, from his last remaining party post, news agencies said.
Nineteen of the 24 members of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) demanded a special meeting of its executive committee be held within 24 hours, they said.
The demand was "part of moves in the campaign for the removal of Mr P.V. Narasimha Rao from the CPP leadership," the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
Rao was prime minister from 1991, when he launched far-reaching economic reforms, until last May when Congress suffered its worst defeat in general elections.

Charged in three separate corruption cases, Rao denies any wrongdoing. He stepped down as party leader in September after a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court to face criminal conspiracy charges, but he has retained leadership of the CPP in the face of mounting criticism.
Critics have accused Congress of not doing enough to check corruption in its ranks and of alienating its traditional supporters among low-caste Hindus and minority Moslems.
PTI said the move to remove Rao had won support from three of the party's most senior leaders, including the former chief ministers of Maharashtra and Kerala states.

In an apparent veiled reference to Rao, Congress president Sitaram Kesri told the party's youth wing on Monday: "It is not proper for a person to continue in public life if people are opposed to him."
Only 80 of Congress's 229 legislators, including members of the upper house, turned up at a dinner hosted by Rao on Monday, The Hindustan Times said.

But Rao appeared determined to hold on to the post and to fight to the finish in his legal cases. On Monday, he claimed immunity from prosecution in a bribery case, arguing that he was a member of parliament.

Congress spokesman V.N. Gadgil said Rao would not step down as CPP chief before a meeting of the party's main decision-making body, the Congress Working Committee, set for Wednesday, the United News of India said.
